Chapter 8

Introduction to Trigonometry

Exam weight: 7 marks (2 VSA + 1 SA-I + 1 SA-II) | Dropped: Trigonometric Ratios of Complementary Angles

Concept Notes

  • In a right triangle, for acute angle θ: sinθ = opposite/hyp, cosθ = adjacent/hyp, tanθ = opposite/adjacent (and their reciprocals cosecθ, secθ, cotθ).
  • Standard values at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° must be known by heart.
  • Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1,   1 + tan²θ = sec²θ,   1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

VSA (1 mark) — 10 Qs

  1. If sinA = 3/5, find cosA (A acute).
  2. If cosA = 12/13, find tanA.
  3. Evaluate: 2 sin30° cos30°.
  4. If tanθ = 1, find θ (0° < θ < 90°).
  5. If √3 tanθ = 1, find θ.
  6. Evaluate: sin²60° + cos²60°.
  7. If cotθ = 7/24, find cosecθ.
  8. If 3tanθ = 4, find sinθ + cosθ (θ acute).
  9. Evaluate: sin60°cos30° + cos60°sin30°.
  10. If secθ = 13/12, find sinθ.

SA-I (2 marks) — 6 Qs (right-triangle ratio problems / standard-angle evaluations)

  1. In ΔABC, ∠B = 90°, tanA = 3/4, BC = 6 cm. Find AC and sinC. (see Fig. 1)
  2. In ΔPQR, ∠Q = 90°, cosP = 5/13, PR = 26 cm. Find QR and tanR. (see Fig. 2)
  3. Evaluate: (4/3)(sin²60° + cos²60°) + 2tan45°.
  4. If sinθ = 8/17, find cosθ and cotθ. (see Fig. 3)
  5. Evaluate: 3cos²30° − 2sin²45° + tan²60°.
  6. In ΔLMN, ∠M = 90°, tanL = 5/12, LM = 24 cm. Find MN and secL. (see Fig. 4)

SA-II (3 marks) — 8 Qs — Prove the identity

  1. (sinθ + cosθ)² + (sinθ − cosθ)² = 2
  2. cotθ + tanθ = secθ cosecθ
  3. (1 − sinθ)/(1 + sinθ) = (secθ − tanθ)²
  4. sinθ/(1+cosθ) + (1+cosθ)/sinθ = 2cosecθ
  5. (1+tanθ)² + (1−tanθ)² = 2sec²θ
  6. (cosecθ − sinθ)(secθ − cosθ)(tanθ + cotθ) = 1
  7. tan²θ − sin²θ = tan²θ sin²θ
  8. (1+secθ−tanθ)/(1+secθ+tanθ) = (1−sinθ)/cosθ

Chapter 9

Some Applications of Trigonometry (Heights & Distances)

Exam weight: 3 marks — only ever tested as 1 SA-II question

Concept Notes

  • Draw a clear right-triangle diagram for every problem — label the angle of elevation/depression, height, and horizontal distance.
  • Angle of elevation: measured upward from horizontal. Angle of depression: measured downward from horizontal (equals the elevation angle from the lower point, by alternate angles).
  • Choose the correct ratio (tan is most common) relating the known side to the unknown side.

SA-II (3 marks) — 8 Qs — Word Problems

  1. A ladder's foot is 6 m from a wall and it makes an angle of 60° with the ground. Find the length of the ladder. (see Fig. 1)
  2. From a point on the ground 20 m from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top is 30°. Find the height of the tower. (see Fig. 2)
  3. A kite is flying at a height of 60 m, attached to a string inclined at 60° to the horizontal. Find the length of the string. (see Fig. 3)
  4. The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 50 m from its base is 45°. Find the height of the tower. (see Fig. 4)
  5. From the top of a building 15 m high, the angle of depression of a car on the ground is 30°. Find the distance of the car from the base of the building. (see Fig. 5)
  6. From the top of a cliff 100 m high, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a tower are 30° and 60° respectively. Find the height of the tower. (see Fig. 6)
  7. Two poles of equal height stand on either side of a road 80 m wide. From a point on the road between them, the angles of elevation of their tops are 60° and 30°. Find the height of the poles and the distances of the point from each pole. (see Fig. 7)
  8. From the top of a tower 50√3 m high, the angle of depression of a car on the ground is 30°. Find the distance of the car from the base of the tower. (see Fig. 8)
